Cloud Sync
This sends patient data to your own Supabase project so it stays in sync across your PC, Mac and your assistant's device. Nothing leaves this device until you enter your keys and sign in — the app works fully offline otherwise.

1 · Connect your project

2 · Sign in

Create the login for yourself and your assistant in Supabase → Authentication → Users. Both sign in here on their own device.

3 · Sync

Two-way sync merges records (never deletes). Your assistant's new entries appear here, and yours on his device.

📡 How often devices talk to each other

Supabase's free plan allows two million realtime messages a month, and it counts one for every device that receives an update — so a single change with three devices connected costs three or four. This is where that budget goes.

One-time database setup

After creating your project, open Supabase → SQL Editor → New query, paste this, and press Run. (Full step-by-step guide is in the chat.)

🔒 Unlock with Face ID or a fingerprint

Uses the phone's own Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint instead of typing your password on this device. Your password still works and never changes. Nothing about this is synced — switch it on separately on each phone or computer.

♿ Accessibility

These settings are kept on this device and take effect straight away.

Text size lives on the left-hand bar (A− / A+). Press Tab at the top of any page for a “skip to the main content” link.

📱 The bar at the bottom of your phone

Four places you can reach with your thumb, without opening any menu. Tap to choose which four — the newest choice replaces the oldest. Everything else stays one tap away under More. This only shows on a phone.

📱 Install as an app

Puts the clinic on your home screen. It opens full-screen (no browser bars) and keeps working with no internet — nothing else to set up.

iPhone / iPad: tap Share ▸ Add to Home Screen.  Android / computer: tap Install app above (or your browser’s menu ▸ Install).

Users & access

Everyone signs in with their email and password — the same login works on all their devices. You are the owner 👑. Anyone who joins with your invite stays pending until you approve them, and you choose exactly what each person can see (per section: no access, view only or can edit). Income, Analytics, Settings & Cloud Sync always stay with you.

🗂 Google Drive — where the full-resolution files live

Every image you attach to a tumour registry case is kept here in a compressed copy so the app stays fast, while the untouched original is uploaded to your Drive. “View complete record” opens that case's folder. The app is only ever given access to folders and files it created itself — it cannot see the rest of your Drive.

Where a file actually ends up
1 · The original, full resolution → your Google Drive, in this case's folder. Until it gets there it waits in this browser and is marked Queued; once Drive confirms it, the local copy of the original is deleted.
2 · A compressed copy + thumbnail → this device only, in the browser's own store, so the record opens instantly and works offline. These are not uploaded to Supabase and not synced — on your other devices the app shows a Drive placeholder and opens the original.
3 · The index — file names, sizes, dates, your follow-up notes and the Drive links → the registry entry itself, which does sync through Supabase to your other devices.
So: Supabase carries the paperwork, Drive carries the pictures, this device keeps a fast copy. If Drive is not set up, nothing leaves this device — the originals simply stay here, which is why the badge says Local.

Folders are made for you, once per case:
Clinic Case Files / 2601010001 — Ahmed Khan / 01 Pre-op docs · 02 Pre-op planning · 03 Intra-op · 04 Post-op · 05 Histopathology · 06 Follow-up / 8-52

📷 Image compression

A phone photograph arrives at 3–8 MB. The copy kept on this device is shrunk so a hundred cases still open instantly and sync quickly; the original is what goes to Drive. Plain films are detected automatically and treated more gently than clinical photographs, because JPEG throws away exactly the faint grey detail a fracture line lives in.

💾 Storage space

How much of this device’s local storage your records are using. X-ray images don’t count here — they’re kept in a separate large store. When this gets high, export a backup and archive old years, or ask me to upgrade the storage.

Backup & data

Everything is saved automatically in this browser on this computer. The backup file restores all patients, visits, medicines, documents and settings. X-ray images are kept in a separate large store — use “Export images” below to back those up too.

Auto-backup keeps one backup file continuously up to date — every save silently rewrites it. Choose a file inside your Google Drive or iCloud folder and your data is cloud-backed with zero effort. (Chrome may ask once per session to allow access — one click.)

With a password set, backup files (manual and auto) are AES-encrypted — safe even if your Google Drive is compromised. You'll be asked for this password when restoring. Write it down: a lost password means the backup cannot be opened by anyone.

X-ray images are stored separately from records — export them here to move or safeguard them.
